rich_summary: This section recounts the final moments and funeral of Bhishma after completing his long discourse on duty. Granted permission by Krishna, Bhishma consciously releases his life through yogic control, directing his life‑breath upward until it exits through the crown of his head and ascends to heaven, accompanied by celestial signs and praise from sages and gods. The Pandavas and elders perform his funeral rites with royal honors and cremate his body. Afterwards they go to the Ganges to offer libations. The river‑goddess Ganga rises from the waters, grieving for her son and recalling his unmatched valor and virtue. Krishna consoles her, reminding her that Bhishma was one of the divine Vasus who merely took human birth due to a curse and has now returned to the highest realm. The episode closes the Anusasana Parva, emphasizing Bhishma’s sanctity, mastery over death, and his transition from heroic warrior to immortal exemplar of dharma.

highlight_spans.why: Bhishma seeks Krishna’s permission to cast off his body, marking the decisive moment when he prepares to choose the time of his death.
Krishna praises Bhishma’s flawless life and devotion, explaining why death itself obeys his will.
Bhishma’s final counsel urging devotion to truth and reverence for righteous Brahmanas captures the ethical core of his teachings.
Description of Bhishma using yogic control to withdraw his life‑breaths and release them through the crown of the head—a powerful spiritual climax.
Ganga’s lament for her fallen son expresses the emotional aftermath of the great hero’s death.

top_scenes.scene_text: Bhishma lying on his bed of arrows as radiant sages and Krishna watch while his life‑breath rises upward through the crown of his head like a meteor toward heaven.
The Pandavas performing Bhishma’s royal cremation, surrounding the sandalwood pyre with white yak‑tail fans, garlands, and sacred chants.
The river‑goddess Ganga emerging from the waters of the Bhagirathi, weeping as she laments the loss of her heroic son before Krishna and the gathered kings.
